output.week_summary: This week's strongest material shows how WIA makes an ads recommendation: understand why couples choose the business, look closely at the experience after the click, and support the next sales conversation. I'd develop ranks 1, 3 and 2 as the three Instagram pieces, with rank 2 carrying the week's offer CTA. Rank 4 is an additional process direction worth keeping for development. The proposed surveys and AI widget testing stay clearly separate from current offer features, and the prospect's budget and learning preferences stay internal.

angles.title: A great review still leaves me with a question: why did they book?
angles.audience: Wedding business owners with strong reviews who want their ads to communicate more of what makes couples choose them.
angles.core_perspective: When we're writing wedding ads, I want to know what made a couple choose you as well as what they loved afterward. Those are different parts of the story, and the reason they booked gives us something more specific to say to the next couple.
angles.why_it_matters: This shows the thinking behind WIA's customer research. It puts Whitney's belief into practice: "The best results rarely come from one thing. They're created when visibility, positioning, trust, messaging, and user experience are all aligned." An owner who feels their reviews already tell the story can see why WIA also wants to understand the buying decision.
angles.wia_in_action: Whitney described asking ELEVATE clients for buying research, shared that WIA had begun surveying its own new clients, and explained the VAULT training she had taught on this distinction. She then proposed collecting clients' couples' buying insights and using them to inform ad and landing-page copy.
angles.offer_connection: Shows the depth of WIA's messaging research and the thinking shared with Accelerator members. No offer CTA.
evidence_points: Whitney said ELEVATE clients were directing the team to reviews when asked for actual buying research.
WIA had begun sending surveys to its own new clients to uncover buying triggers.
Whitney described a VAULT training about using buyer types and buying triggers to strengthen ads and landing pages.
She proposed post-booking surveys for ELEVATE clients, with responses shared through a spreadsheet and fed back into copy. This was a proposal.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission to use the call and keep client examples anonymous.
Present the client survey and shared spreadsheet as a proposal, not a standard LeadLock feature.
angles.why_selected: This is the clearest founder point of view in the week. It shows why WIA asks deeper questions without diminishing the value of reviews or framing owners as behind. The research scene is distinct from the recently published measurement and Instagram case studies.

angles.title: What we want couples to feel before they arrive for a venue tour
angles.audience: Venue owners who want the interest generated by their ads to carry into more meaningful tour conversations.
angles.core_perspective: The days before a venue tour give couples time to picture their wedding with you. We build pre-tour nurture through LeadLock and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage to support that decision, alongside the personal conversations your team has with them.
angles.why_it_matters: WIA's move was to look beyond the inquiry and consider what could help a couple stay connected before visiting. It demonstrates Whitney's belief that great marketing "doesn't just give people information. It gives people a future they can see themselves in." For an owner who sees the tour confirmation as the main job of pre-tour emails, this makes the value of thoughtful nurture more concrete.
angles.wia_in_action: The venue owner described already reaching out personally to couples with tours booked farther ahead. Whitney suggested adding an earlier phone or virtual preview. Fallon Looney, who is no longer with WIA, proposed a supplemental wedding-video email for couples with a longer wait before their tour.
angles.offer_connection: LeadLock and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage include done-for-you email and text workflows, including pre-consult nurture. Use this scene to illustrate the thinking behind that work, while keeping the owner's personal follow-up central. Place the week's single offer CTA here, inviting owners to inquire about LeadLock.
evidence_points: The owner identified longer waits before tours as a possible factor in cancellations and described her existing personal outreach to offer an earlier visit.
Whitney asked whether the venue offered virtual tours before suggesting an earlier personal connection.
Whitney proposed a phone conversation or virtual behind-the-scenes preview, potentially on a wedding day if the team had bandwidth.
Fallon proposed a supplemental email with wedding video and an invitation to ask questions for couples whose tours were farther out.
The call contains recommendations, not evidence that these changes were implemented or improved tour attendance.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission and anonymize the venue; exclude its private conversion and cancellation figures.
Credit Whitney's preview suggestion separately from former team member Fallon's email idea, and keep both as recommendations.
angles.why_selected: This earns a LeadLock invitation through a specific sales moment. The point is the purpose of nurture, rather than a reminder checklist or a claim that automation handles the sale. It is stronger than a generic tour-attendance lesson because WIA's diagnosis and recommendations are visible.

angles.title: Why Carmen wanted to see more before judging this venue's campaign
angles.audience: Wedding business owners investing in ads who want to understand how a strategist decides what to change and when.
angles.core_perspective: When we review a venue's campaign, we consider how much evidence we have and what people do after they click. Carmen checked visitor behavior and the page itself, identified details worth reviewing, and kept the bigger campaign verdict open.
angles.why_it_matters: This is WIA's diagnosis beyond the dashboard in practice. It supports Whitney's belief that "good marketing decisions start with good data." For an owner looking for a clear next move, it shows why a useful recommendation can include a focused adjustment, another specialist's review and more observation before a larger change.
angles.wia_in_action: Carmen reviewed a venue's corporate-event campaign during office hours. She considered the limited click data, looked at visitor behavior, checked the page herself and noticed a wedding banner. When the owner identified additional sitelinks, Carmen said she would remove them. She also recommended asking Jacqueline for landing-page feedback and said she did not yet have a conclusion about why visitors weren't proceeding.
angles.offer_connection: Demonstrates the reasoning and account-specific feedback available through WIA's guided support. Keep this trust-building piece free of an offer CTA.
evidence_points: Carmen said the campaign needed more room to gather evidence before she could judge it.
She distinguished short visits from visitors spending time on the page without proceeding.
The owner identified sitelinks being added to the ad; Carmen said she would take them out.
Carmen observed a wedding banner on the corporate-event page and reviewed a visitor's movement around the inquiry form.
She recommended a landing-page review from Jacqueline and explicitly left the cause unresolved.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission and identify this accurately as a venue's corporate-event campaign; omit private performance figures.
Don't imply the sitelinks were removed, Jacqueline completed a review or a cause was confirmed.
angles.why_selected: The distinctive contribution is Carmen's judgment about the evidence, including what she could not yet conclude. This differs from the recent attribution case study: the point is how WIA reaches a recommendation, rather than proving that bookings can be measured.

angles.title: How we decide whether to refine your campaigns or build again
angles.audience: Wedding business owners who have already invested time in Google campaigns and want expert direction for their next stage of growth.
angles.core_perspective: When you've already put work into your ads, we want to understand the campaigns and landing pages together. What we find should guide whether we refine the setup or recommend a new search campaign.
angles.why_it_matters: This makes WIA's diagnosis-before-recommendation approach visible. It reflects Whitney's belief that "good marketing decisions start with good data." An owner who expects hiring an ads specialist to mean starting over can see that WIA's recommendation should come from examining the work already in place.
angles.wia_in_action: The prospect asked for a review of existing campaigns and landing pages. Whitney outlined a review with Carmen covering both, then explained that a Google Search Accelerator recommendation could follow if Carmen found that a new search campaign or substantial landing-page work was appropriate. No review or final recommendation happened in this excerpt.
angles.offer_connection: Makes the reasoning behind a Google Search Accelerator recommendation concrete. Its current scope is a campaign built and launched by WIA at a VIP Day, followed by three months of support for the owner. Keep this piece focused on the recommendation process, with no offer CTA or standalone audit promotion.
evidence_points: The prospect described existing campaigns and separate wedding and corporate landing pages, and wanted them examined together.
Whitney said Carmen could review the campaign setup and landing pages in real time.
Whitney made a possible Google Search Accelerator recommendation conditional on what Carmen would find.
The excerpt does not show an audit taking place, an application, enrollment or an outcome.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission and remove the prospect's identity, budget situation and pricing reactions.
Check current wording for this review process; exclude the historical standalone audit arrangement and fee-credit terms.
angles.why_selected: The sales call deserves a public process treatment as well as internal notes. This direction shows how WIA thinks about existing work without turning the prospect's objections into advice. Its central point is choosing the appropriate next step, distinct from Carmen's live campaign diagnosis in rank 3.

internal_insights.insight: Whitney proposed a feedback loop from newly booked couples to a spreadsheet that both the owner and WIA could see, then back into ads and landing pages. The owner would still need to tag contacts or send the survey. Fallon supported the idea, but the scene does not establish implementation.
internal_insights.use: Evaluate the survey questions, owner responsibilities and response-sharing workflow before describing this as a client capability. This extends WIA's customer research process and its belief that positioning, trust, messaging and user experience work together.

internal_insights.insight: The owner contributed the hypothesis about longer tour waits and described real scheduling limits and existing personal outreach. WIA responded with options that could build familiarity before the in-person visit. The call did not establish that the wait caused cancellations.
internal_insights.use: Use this to shape client discovery around the inquiry-to-tour experience, including available tour times, family involvement and existing outreach. Keep the private figures and operational details internal, and test any proposed segmentation rather than treating it as a proven fix.

internal_insights.insight: Carmen wanted more click evidence before judging this particular campaign and did not claim to have found the reason visitors weren't proceeding. She proposed a sitelink change and a review from Jacqueline.
internal_insights.use: Record the click threshold as an account-specific judgment, not a public benchmark or universal rule. Check whether the proposed changes and page review happened before using any later outcome. The WIA move is disciplined diagnosis, supported by the belief that good marketing decisions start with good data.

internal_insights.insight: Danielle identified missing knowledge-base answers as a limit on evaluating the proposed AI widget. Whitney asked Gisselle to prepare WIA's own knowledge base for her review, preferred testing in WIA's account first and wanted to think carefully about the sales handoff. No client rollout or working feature was established.
internal_insights.use: Keep this in product evaluation. Document the required information, founder review and human handoff before assessing readiness. Whitney's belief that automation should enhance the sales process, not replace it, is relevant to that evaluation. Do not describe the widget as a current LeadLock feature or as AI talking to couples.

internal_insights.insight: The prospect wanted hands-on, account-specific help and asked who would make changes. He also expressed a preference for hands-on learning over reading and watching materials.
internal_insights.use: Use this to make responsibility and support clear in qualifying conversations: WIA builds and launches Accelerator campaigns, then guides the owner. Ask about preferred ways of working without recasting the Accelerator as a course or ongoing management.

internal_insights.insight: The prospect asked about performance-based management, flexible pricing and a narrower starting point. Whitney held the management model boundary and discussed a historical review arrangement. The prospect's budget situation is not suitable public content.
internal_insights.use: Keep this for sales-fit research and current-offer checks. Do not publish prices, promote the historical arrangement or turn the prospect's reaction into advice that invites doubt about WIA's offers.

considered_not_selected.idea: How we could bring newly booked couples' answers back into their venue's ads
considered_not_selected.reason: The proposed research loop is worth developing internally, but a separate public card would overlap rank 1 and depend on an implementation the scene does not establish.

considered_not_selected.idea: A virtual preview for couples waiting longer for their venue tour
considered_not_selected.reason: The specific recommendation is good evidence for rank 2. As a standalone piece, it would become a venue sales tactic and leave WIA's broader nurture thinking in the background.

considered_not_selected.idea: Our Accelerator support brings more than one set of eyes to your ads
considered_not_selected.reason: Carmen's referral to Jacqueline supports the idea, but the excerpt only shows a recommended review. Rank 3 gives this scene more substance by showing Carmen's actual reasoning, with the referral as supporting evidence.

considered_not_selected.idea: How many clicks to wait for before judging a Google campaign
considered_not_selected.reason: The threshold was Carmen's judgment for this account. Publishing it as a general rule would overstate the evidence and turn a strategic scene into basic benchmark advice.

considered_not_selected.idea: Why we test new sales tools in our own business first
considered_not_selected.reason: The decision has a useful WIA point of view, but this example concerns an unconfirmed AI widget. A public treatment could imply a current client feature or conflict with LeadLock's approved description. Keep the scene in product evaluation.

considered_not_selected.idea: Promote a standalone Google review as an entry point to the Accelerator
considered_not_selected.reason: The historical arrangement is not a current public offer in the offer sheet. Rank 4 preserves the diagnostic thinking without promoting its old terms or using the prospect's pricing reaction.

pillar_notes.note: Rank 1 provides the founder opinion for reach. It values reviews while showing why WIA also asks about the decision to book.

Ranks 3 and 4 show two different parts of WIA's reasoning: how much a live campaign review can establish, and how existing work informs the recommended next step. Develop rank 3 first; rank 4 can remain in the content bank.

Rank 2 is the sole offer-CTA piece. Publish it after the research and diagnosis pieces so the LeadLock invitation follows a clear demonstration of WIA's thinking. For the three-piece week, use ranks 1, 3 and 2. A Tuesday email can carry rank 3's insight without an offer CTA or Instagram references.
